result.architecture_summary: The repository contains four largely disconnected layers: assignment-era agent/RAG/GER prototypes; an elaborate global reconciliation and verification system; a deterministic but read-only 37-item bootstrap graph; and a documented future supervisor/context/validation architecture. The core bounded-worker and evidence-gate ideas are sound, but there is no functioning ticket-to-Unity delivery loop. The architecture currently automates planning about the game much more than production of the game.
result.verdict_reason: The conceptual split between durable state, bounded workers, deterministic checks, runtime evidence, and human design authority is sound. The implemented control plane is not: it is bootstrap-centric, cannot legitimately evolve the graph, uses stale RAG data, does not enforce merged completion, and has no bridge from a ready task to an isolated worker or Unity validation. Its milestone order has produced severe infrastructure displacement: after Assignment 6, 147 first-parent commits reached the frozen commit without any change under Assets/. This should be reorganized, not discarded wholesale.
strong_decisions: Integrated main should remain authority for implemented game state; an agent must not declare itself complete.
Deterministic graph validation and dependency readiness are appropriate uses of local code.
Runtime evidence overriding static approval directly addresses the demonstrated camera failures.
Structured feedback, no-op detection, bounded repair, and circuit breakers are valuable once wrapped around real ticket execution.
One reliable worker before parallelism is the correct sequencing.
Separating design-gap detection from unauthorized design generation is sensible, although the full artifact platform is premature.
Isolated branches/worktrees are an appropriate eventual execution boundary.
structural_flaws: The current machinery stops at `taskcontrol ready`; it cannot dispatch, claim, execute, validate, merge, complete, invalidate, supersede, or reopen a task.

`work_graph_validate.py` requires every task to contain bootstrap provenance and requires one shared provenance pair across all tasks. Legitimate later tasks from a new GDD revision cannot represent their actual provenance.
The validator requires IDs to form a contiguous range tied to task count. This is bootstrap-oriented rather than lifecycle-oriented and makes retirement/deletion semantics awkward.
ADR-026 depends on a deterministic reconciliation diff/review/apply boundary, but neither `taskcontrol` nor another implemented component provides it.
`status` only supports `open` and `complete`. There is no `needs_review`, `superseded`, `cancelled`, or `invalidated` state for evolving canon.
Done-means-merged is documented but unenforced. The graph loader trusts a manually edited `complete` value without checking merge ancestry, task evidence, tests, or affected files.

The GDD conflates product design, runtime ownership, pipeline architecture, token/schedule policy, and dated repository observations. Treating all of this as root canon creates self-referential reconciliation churn.

The current RAG corpus predates extensive GDD changes and lacks source-content hash validation. Reusing it for NSC-003 would omit the newer mouse movement, shared-pointer, suspension, Tilemap, and navigation requirements.
Immutable reconciliation directories are not fully reproducible snapshots: the reconciliation artifact records source paths but not the observed Git commit or GDD content hash.

The destructive central scene builder is a growing integration bottleneck. Many future tasks claim both it and the canonical scene, and generated rebuilds may eventually conflict with human-authored scene content.
observed_failure_solutions: The persistent graph improves on the actually stale Assignment 5 goal artifacts: those still select the camera, while the graph correctly records the integrated camera as complete.
Assignment 6 runtime feedback solves an actual Unity failure: the camera passed static review twice while facing/framing gameplay incorrectly.
The GER no-op progress guard solves an actual failure where the Refiner claimed success without changing Assets/.
The Assignment 4 critic/revision loop addresses actual unsupported content drift; its first critic marked 8 of 13 items for revision.
Independent reconciliation verification addressed real candidate defects: the recorded bootstrap process began with 21 material findings before refinement.
Append-only feedback and resume/recovery paths address interrupted reconciliation, timeout, identity, source-boundary, and synthesis failures visible in history.
Scene-builder regression tests address the actual door progress-fill defect found only after human playtesting.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Artifact Authority and Artifact GER have no real task or approved artifact exercising them; the bootstrap contains zero artifact records.
Progressive Decomposition has not resolved a real near-frontier blockage.
Parallel resource claims, leases, merge queues, and multiple workers protect against concurrency that is explicitly deferred.
GitHub Projects mirroring solves future dashboard needs, not the present absence of ticket execution.
A generic scanner cache and Roslyn-level analysis are speculative; NSC-003 names the small set of relevant files already.
Continuous backlog replenishment and autonomous scheduling are premature before one ticket can complete.

Multi-stream field repair, conflict arbitration, extensive model-role diversity, and architecture-review orchestration mostly protect the reconciliation platform from its own complexity rather than accelerate Unity production.
overengineering: From Assignment 6 to the frozen commit, 147 first-parent commits made no changes under Assets/; 56 touched reconciliation.
The same interval added roughly 96,000 lines across pipeline/review areas and no gameplay diff.

Pipeline/Reconciliation contains about 10,275 top-level Python lines and approximately 88,420 lines including committed documentation/output artifacts, compared with roughly 3,721 lines across game C#, scenes, and asmdefs.

A 37-record bootstrap produced candidates, raw candidates, merged candidates, two audit passes, stream repairs, conflict arbitration, refined candidates, rendered variants, current views, approval hashes, bootstrap metadata, and task copies.
The eight-role architecture-review runner is itself another sizable autonomous pipeline added before game-production leverage has been demonstrated.
The architecture documents appropriately warn against speculative infrastructure, but repository investment has already violated that guidance.
missing_components: A supported live-task mutation API with per-change provenance and atomic validation.
Stable GDD requirement IDs plus requirement-level hashes or versions.
Targeted GDD change-impact analysis across tasks, approved artifacts, files, tests, and active runs.
A generic bridge from one task contract to an isolated coding worker.
Restartable run state for real ticket execution, distinct from reconciliation recovery.
Automated Unity compilation, EditMode, PlayMode, and Windows build validation on a Unity-capable machine.
A task-specific runtime/playtest rubric and structured capture mechanism.
Merge-aware completion and automatic reopening/invalidation when acceptance criteria change.
Basic throughput telemetry: elapsed time, model time, human minutes, retries, runtime defects, and false approvals.
A production Unity asset-ownership strategy beyond continually expanding one destructive prototype scene builder.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundary: versioned game-design requirements define desired player behavior.
Necessary boundary: engineering ADRs define implementation/process constraints and should not be embedded as game-design canon.
Necessary boundary: integrated main defines actual implementation state.
Necessary boundary: small task contracts define intended deltas and acceptance evidence.
Necessary boundary: run/test/playtest records define execution and validation evidence.
Necessary boundary: humans retain authority over design changes, subjective quality, architecture exceptions, and release acceptance.

Reconciliation snapshots, raw/refined candidates, graph deltas, current views, approved bootstrap records, and Tasks duplicate planning semantics. Keep immutable audit results, but make one task store the operational authority.
GitHub should remain an optional view of execution, not another required authority, until local ticket execution works.
Approved design artifacts should become an authority class only when a real missing design artifact blocks work.
Task completion currently duplicates main without an enforced synchronization mechanism.
The GDD's dated repository inventory and pipeline constraints duplicate CURRENT_STATE, ADRs, Git, and task metadata; these should be split out.
gdd_iteration_concerns: A GDD edit currently leaves the RAG corpus, open tasks, completed tasks, context packs, tests, and in-flight branches silently stale.
A whole-document hash is useful for cache invalidation but insufficient for impact analysis; stable requirement IDs and per-requirement versions are needed.
When an open task's requirement changes, pause active execution, revise or supersede its contract, and require design-owner approval before resuming.
When completed behavior changes, preserve historical completion but create a migration/regression task or reopen the capability; do not rewrite old run history.
When a requirement is removed, cancel or supersede unstarted work and explicitly decide whether implemented code should be removed.
When a changed requirement conflicts with an approved artifact, mark that artifact untrusted for affected downstream work until reviewed.
Routine edits should inspect only changed requirements and linked tasks/files/tests. Full reconciliation should be a periodic milestone audit or recovery tool.
The current statuses cannot express any of these transitions.
The stale Assignment 4 corpus demonstrates that synchronization with evolving canon is already an observed problem, not a hypothetical future concern.
result.throughput_assessment: Major near-term leverage is plausible from bounded coding agents, deterministic tests, and compact task contracts, but not from the current architecture as integrated. The AgentCrew produced its first door implementation in about 13 minutes of recorded agent time, showing meaningful generation speed, but human playtesting found a visual defect and triggered multiple repair/review passes. Assignment 6 required repeated human Unity cycles and exhausted all three refinements. Those are useful experiments, not evidence of weeks becoming days. If additional infrastructure were forbidden, the first failure would be that `taskcontrol ready` has no execution bridge: a human must assemble context, invoke the worker, manage Git, run Unity, feed back failures, merge, and edit task status. After manual dispatch, Unity runtime judgment would be the first unavoidable bottleneck. Automate branch/run bookkeeping and repeatable Unity commands after this slice; retain human play-feel and design judgment.
human_intervention_points: Select priorities and approve material GDD changes.
Scrub generated task contracts for duplication, ambiguity, and excessive scope before execution.
Manually assemble context and invoke a worker until a thin ticket runner exists.
Create/manage the branch or worktree and resolve shared Unity asset conflicts.
Run or inspect Unity scene, prefab, package, Input Actions, and build integration where batch evidence is unavailable.
Judge movement feel, camera framing, readability, art direction, balance, and whether the feature is fun.
Convert runtime observations into actionable feedback when automated tests cannot express them.
Approve scope expansion, architecture changes, missing design, and failed circuit-breaker escalations.
Review and merge changes until the pipeline's false-positive rate is measured.
Worth automating next, if repeated: context extraction, branch/run journaling, Unity batch commands, evidence bundling, and merge-aware task completion.
Not worth automating away: product intent, subjective play quality, architecture exceptions, and release acceptance.

next_slice.title: Deliver NSC-003 end to end without building Milestone 2 as a platform
next_slice.why: It is real visible gameplay, already dependency-ready, foundational to doors and spells, and exercises Input Actions, shared targeting, scene integration, automated tests, runtime feel, repair, Git integration, and graph completion. It also tests whether the graph's `single_agent` classification is truthful. No Progressive Decomposer, artifact system, generic scanner, or stale RAG corpus is needed.
deliverables: Perform a short human contract scrub: remove the duplicate suspension criterion and bind the run to the current GDD commit/hash.

Manually create one isolated branch/worktree and assemble context directly from NSC-003, its cited current GDD sections, PlayerMovement, Input Actions, scene builder, canonical scene, and relevant tests.
Implement Input Actions-based click/hold mouse movement, one shared cursor-to-gameplay-plane projection, movement restriction request/release, reset, and suspend/re-enable behavior.
Add deterministic tests for destination movement, live hold steering, shared projection, immediate suspend, restriction, and reset behavior.
Run Unity compile plus relevant EditMode/PlayMode tests on the Unity-capable machine.
Perform one focused human playtest for responsiveness, stopping behavior, projection accuracy, camera compatibility, and interaction regressions.
Feed any blocking runtime result through one bounded repair pass, then revalidate.
Merge only after evidence passes; update task state deliberately and rerun graph validation.
Record elapsed wall time, agent time, human minutes, retries, defects, false passes, changed files, and validation results.
next_slice.proof_of_value: A successful result is NSC-003 merged within one working day, with less than roughly one hour of human orchestration/playtesting, no silent design invention, and reproducible compile/test evidence. Whether it succeeds or fails, the measured first repeated bottleneck—not the current milestone document—determines the next automation slice.

do_not_build_yet: Artifact Authority Gate and artifact promotion store
Generic project scanner/cache or Roslyn service
A regenerated full RAG corpus before a real task demonstrates retrieval need
Claims, leases, parallel workers, or merge queue
More reconciliation auditor roles, streaming repair, or conflict arbitration
A generic evaluator marketplace or extensive style pipeline integration

alternative_architecture.description: Reorganize around a change-driven feature conveyor. State: keep product requirements in versioned Markdown with stable IDs and per-requirement hashes; keep engineering ADRs and current repository facts separate; use small task contracts linked to requirement IDs; let main and test/run evidence determine completion. Planning: a human selects the next product outcome and one planner proposes one to three vertical slices; ordinary GDD diffs target only linked work; run global reconciliation only at milestones or when drift is suspected. Execution: a small restartable coordinator creates one worktree, builds context through direct requirement/file extraction, invokes one bounded coding worker, and journals the run. Validation: run cheap Git/static checks, Unity compile, EditMode/PlayMode tests, Windows build checks when relevant, a task-specific runtime rubric, and a fresh semantic diff review. Recovery: retry once or twice from structured evidence, retain the branch/run record, then escalate; do not add streaming multi-agent refinement unless repeated failures justify it. Unity integration: use production prefabs and serialized scene assets as owned integration surfaces, keep scripted scene builders primarily for reproducible fixtures, and require human review for authored scene/prefab changes. Completion: merge, append evidence, update the linked task, and recompute readiness. GDD changes invalidate only affected contexts/tasks/artifacts and create explicit migration work for completed behavior.
alternative_architecture.why_better: This preserves the sound ideas—durable state, bounded workers, deterministic computation, runtime evidence, recovery, and human authority—while replacing global reconciliation as the center of gravity with actual feature flow. It handles moving canon as routine incremental synchronization, reduces duplicate state, exposes throughput immediately, and postpones automation until a repeated human cost is observed.

evidence.observation: Implements only validate, list, show, ready, and graph. There is no execution, mutation, completion, invalidation, claim, or reconciliation-delta command.
Requires `bootstrap_source` on every task, enforces one common bootstrap provenance pair, and requires a contiguous ID range based on current task count.
When Tasks exist, it returns `taskcontrol_diff_required` and empty proposed changes, deferring to a diff/apply workflow that is not implemented.
Records source paths but no frozen source commit or GDD content hash, weakening its claimed point-in-time provenance.
Identifies a July 30 final draft and was last changed August 6.
Changed repeatedly through August 21 and now contains requirements absent from the RAG corpus, including mouse-directed movement, shared projection, suspend contracts, Tilemaps, and AI Navigation.
Root canon includes agent roles, pipeline rules, token budgets, Git workflow, and dated repository evidence alongside game design.
Contains broad prose evidence, no stable requirement IDs/GDD hash, and duplicates the gameplay-suspension acceptance criterion.
Documents two static camera passes that failed human Unity runtime validation and a third no-op refinement before the final repair.
Ends at `accepted_static`; all three refinements were used and the circuit breaker is marked tripped. Final Unity approval exists only in human-authored documentation.
Shows rapid initial door implementation, followed by human-discovered progress-UI failure and additional repair/review passes requiring Unity retesting.
The strongest camera and UI regression coverage was added only after runtime failures clarified what static criteria missed.
Acts as a central destructive scene construction/wiring surface claimed by many planned tasks.
Contains about 10,275 top-level Python lines and extensive committed multi-pass outputs, repairs, conflicts, recovery, and current-view copies.
147 first-parent commits followed Assignment 6; zero touched Assets, while 56 touched Pipeline/Reconciliation.
Approximately 96,000 lines were added across pipeline/review areas with no gameplay asset change.
`python3 Pipeline/TaskGraph/taskcontrol.py validate` passes and returns seven ready tasks, confirming the deterministic graph works for inspection but not that it can deliver one.

result.biggest_uncertainty: The repository lacks consistent human-time, cost, and end-to-end lead-time measurements, and this review environment cannot independently rerun the documented Unity editor/runtime validations.
